issues.description: The problem statement inconsistently refers to the animal feeding method as getFeedingSound() in several places (e.g., instructions for Seal/Pig/Goat and feedAllAnimals description), while the UML, tasks, and the provided solution use the method name messageOnFeed(). This mismatch in the method name/signature will confuse students about which method they must implement and use (messageOnFeed() vs getFeedingSound()).
issues.suggestedFix: Make the method name consistent across all artifacts. Either (A) change all occurrences of getFeedingSound() in the problem statement to messageOnFeed(), matching the UML and solution, or (B) update UML, template, and solution to use getFeedingSound() consistently. Update the example text for feedAllAnimals() and the Seal/Pig/Goat instructions accordingly so students implement and call the same method name.

issues.description: The problem statement inconsistently refers to the feeding-sound method as both messageOnFeed() (in the UML and Part 1) and getFeedingSound() (in Part 2 and the song template). The template and the solution implement and expect messageOnFeed(). This naming mismatch can confuse students about which method to implement and which method to call when building the song verses.
issues.suggestedFix: Unify the naming: replace all occurrences of getFeedingSound() in the problem statement (including the song template examples) with messageOnFeed(), or explicitly state that getFeedingSound() is an alias for messageOnFeed(). Ensure the tasks and song examples consistently reference messageOnFeed() to match the template and solution.
